Subject: Re: Discovery + next steps — token volumes & pricing targets

Hi Sara — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups from our side: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use case: in-product assistant for finance workflows (invoice review, reconciliation suggestions, KYC summaries).
- Target launch: pilot with ~150k MAUs (internal estimate you shared) over first 6 months.
- Usage profile: ~3 sessions/user/month, ~800 tokens/session (avg prompt + response).

From those numbers, estimated monthly token volume (rough):
- 150k users * 3 sessions * 800 tokens = ~360,000,000 tokens/month (~360M)

Open items we promised to follow up on:
1) Target budget range for inference (monthly). You gave a broad range on the call — can you confirm a target monthly spend (e.g., $25k–$75k)?
2) Target $/1M tokens you’re comfortable with for pilot and for scale (we heard ~$30–$50 mentioned).
3) Any constraints on model quality vs cost (i.e., willing to accept a small drop in quality for 30% reduction in cost?).

Next steps
- I attached a simple pricing_model_template.xlsx to help capture your expected MAU, sessions, token mix, and target unit economics. If you can populate the fields we’ll run a quick unit-econ sensitivity and propose recommended model/config (quantization, batching profiles, etc.).
- Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review the populated sheet and go through the unit-econ tradeoffs? Suggested slots: Tue 3/30 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 3/31 9:00–10:00 PT.

Thanks — 
Marissa

Subject: RE: Unit econ deep-dive + pilot recommendations

Perfect — thanks for the numbers, Sara. I ran a quick sensitivity and wanted to share a concise unit-econ framing before our call so we can focus on tradeoffs: 

Unit economics primer (pilot assumptions)
- Monthly tokens: 360M (as discussed).
- Target spend (pilot range): $30k–$60k/month => implied $/1M tokens = $83–$167 (note: that’s unaffordable for scale if volumes grow).

Redwood recommendation (config + target)
- Pilot configuration: curated 13B open model variant with 8-bit quantization + caching for prompt prefixes. Estimated delivered cost: ~$25–$40/1M tokens.
- Scale target: aim for $20–$35/1M tokens through batching, dedicated capacity, and model/quantization tuning.

Mapping to product metrics: $/feature and CAC payback
- Example feature: "Smart reconciliation" engaged by 10% of MAU (15k users) => monthly tokens for feature ~15k * 3 sessions * 800 tokens = 36M tokens => at $30/1M tokens => $1,080/month inference cost for that feature.
- Revenue per user (rough): if revenue per user/month is $5 (ARPU), feature-driven revenue for engaged users = 15k * $5 = $75k/month. Inference cost as % of revenue = $1,080 / $75,000 = 1.4% (very healthy).
- CAC payback: if CAC is $30 and incremental revenue from the feature is $3/user/month, payback = 10 months. We typically recommend < 12 months for PLG-led expansion; best-case target is 6 months.

Margin targets vs inference cost
- Target gross margin: 55–65% for product gross margin. That implies inference should be a small fraction (<10%) of gross margin after other costs.
- For pilot, keep per-1M cost below $40 to achieve reasonable margin headroom as you scale.

Attached is a short one-page unit econ with examples and a filled model from the template (redwood_unit_econ_v1.pdf). We'll walk sensitivity (tokens/session, adoption %) live in the call.

Call: Tue 3/30 10:00 PT — invite sent. Agenda: review filled sheet, pick model config, define success metrics for pilot (SLOs, cost per 1M target, quality thresholds).

Questions for you before the call (quick):
- Can you confirm approximate ARPU or revenue-attributed-to-feature for the pilot cohort (or a proxy)?
- Any procurement/compliance blockers we should prep for (SOC2 evidence, network requirements)?

Thanks — looking forward.
Marissa
